(Mgh.) Said of a man, it means [(assumed tropical:) He lay down: and he sat: or] he sat upon his knees: and it may also mean he sat upon his thighs and his buttocks. (Har p.

172.) 4. ― -b2- rab~aDotuhu biAlmakaAni , inf. n. tarobiyDN , (assumed tropical:) I fixed him, or made him to remain fixed, in the place. (TA.) ― -b2- A^arobaDahumo (tropical:) It (a vessel, S, A, K, and beverage, or wine, A, TA) satisfied their thirst so that they became heavy, and slept, stretched upon the ground: (S, * A, * K:) (tropical:) it (milk) satiated them. : see rabiyDN : in three places.

The lodging-place of sheep or goats; (S, A, * K;) because they lie therein upon their breasts; and in like manner of wild animals: (TA:) the nightly lodging-place of sheep or goats: (Msb:) and ↓ signifies the same: (S, * A, Mgh, Msb:) pl. of the former A^arobaADN : (S, A, * TA:) and of the latter maraAbiDu : (S, K: *) the mrAbD of sheep or goats are like the maEaATin of camels. (S.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A place of abode: a place of abode of a people by itself: (A, TA:) pl. as above. (A.) ― -b3- (tropical:) Anything to which a man betakes himself, or repairs, for lodging, covert, or refuge, (ISk, S, A, * Msb, K,) and at which, or with which, he finds rest, or ease; (K;) such as a house or tent, (S, A, K,) and the like, (S, K,) and a wife, (ISk, S, A, Msb,) or relations, (ISk, A, Msb,) or a fa

[ The winter has come, and I have not yet made for myself ] a lodging: [ O, wo to my two-hands, in consequence of digging ] hollows in which to sit for protection from the cold. (Mgh.) And from rabaDN applied to “ milk which sustains a man, and suffices him for food, ” originated the prov., (K, TA,) minoka rabaDuka waA_ino kaAna samaArFA , meaning (tropical:) Thy family and thy servants (S, K) and those to whom thou betakest thyself for lodging or refuge, (S,) are appertena

[(tropical:) Holding back, through indolence ]. rubuDN Eani AlHaAjaAti , (A, K,) in [some of] the copies of the K, erroneously, EalaY AlHAjAt , (TA,) and AlA^asofaAri , (A, TA,) means (tropical:) A man who does not rise to perform needful affairs, (A, K,) and journeys: (A, TA:) or who does not go forth to undertake them. (Lh, TA.) -A2- See also rabaDN , in three places.

, applied to a man, i q. ↓ ; (K;) i. e. (tropical:) Remaining stationary, and impotent; (TA;) as also ↓ . (K.) -A2- See also riboDapN . ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) A portion, (K,) or large portion, (IDrd,) of variyd [i. e. crumbled bread moistened with broth ]. A mode, or manner, of lying upon the breast: (K, and Har p. 382: [see 1, first signification:]) this is the primary meaning. (Har.) ― -b2- And A place thereof. (Har ibid. [See again rabaDN , first signification.]) ― -b3- See also rabiyDN , in three places. ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) A place of slaughter ( maqotal ) of any party, or company of men, slain in one plot of ground: (Lth, Sgh, K:) erroneously written by Sgh in the TS rabaDap ; but in the O correctly. [And accord. to the TA, it seems to be also applied to (assumed tropical:) The party so slain. ] -A2- Also The body [of an animal] when lying upon the breast; particularly, of a hare, (A, K,) and of a lamb, (A, TA,) and of a she-goat; and so ↓ . : see raAbiDN . ― -b2- Applied to a [skin such as is termed] qirobap , (tropical:) Great, or large; hardly, or not at all, to be lifted; so that it remains fixed

(A, TA.) ― -b3- Then, (A,) applied to a tree ( $ajarap ), meaning (tropical:) Great, or large, (A 'Obeyd, S, A, * K,) and thick, (S,) and, accord. to the K, wide, but [SM says,] I have not seen that any of the leading authorities applies it in this last sense to a tree: (TA:) pl. rubaDN . Sheep, or goats, with their pastors, collected together in their lodging-places; (S, A, K;) as though it were a quasi-pl. n.; as also ↓ and ↓ : (TA:) and hence, (L, TA,) ↓ the former of these two, (assumed tropical:) a company of men: (L, K:) and ↓ the latter of them, [accord. to the K,] a herd of bulls, or cows, in their lodgingplace; from the author of the book entitled kitaAbu Almuzodawiji mina All~ugaAti , only: (K, * TA:) but what this author says is, that ↓ signifies the lodging-places of bulls or cows [app. with the beasts in them ]: and that the primary application of this word ( riboDN ) and ↓ is to sheep or goats; and that by a subsequent usage they have been applied to bulls or cows and to men. (TA.) See also raAbiDN . ― -b2- One says also, Sab~a A@ll~`hu Ealayohi Hum~aY rabiyDF

Lying upon his breast; applied to a sheep or goat [&c.]; and so ↓ applied to a hare; so too ↓ [but app. in an intensive or a frequentative sense] applied to a lion, as is also raAbiDN , and to a man lying on his adversary: (TA:) and [hence] ↓ is an appellation of the lion: (K:) the pl. It is said in a prov., kalobN jaw~aAlN xayorN mino A^asadK raAbiDK or rabaDa [ A dog that roams about is better than a lion lying upon his breast or that has laid himself down upon his breast ]. Hence, because of his cleaving to the ground,] (tropical:) A sick man. [as a subst. from raAbiDN , made so by the affix p , An animal lying upon its breast ]. 3. ― -b2- rabaTa Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) He held back, or drew back, from him, or it; as though he confined, and bound, himself. [In the CK, rabaTa jaA^o$ahu , which would be more properly rendered (tropical:) He strengthened, or fortified, his heart. ]) ― -b4- rabaTa li*`lika AlA^amori jaA^o$FA (tropical:) He constrained himself to be patient, and confined, or restricted, himself to that thing, or affair. 3 signifies, (K, TA,) in its primary acceptation, (TA,) Two [ hostile ] parties' tying of their horses, each at their frontier, and each in preparation for the other: (K, TA:) and ribaATu Alxayoli and muraAbaTatuhaA signify the same [as above]. (S, TA.) [You say, raAbaTa AlfariyqaAni The two parties tied their horses at their respective frontiers, each in preparation for the other. ] And one says, with reference to horses, ↓ , inf. n. raboTN and ribaATN , as well as rAbT , inf. n. muraAbaTapN and ribaATN . Hence, (Sgh, L, K,) rAbT , (Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. ribaATN (S, Mgh, Sgh, L, K) and muraAbaTapN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He, or it, (an army, Mgh) kept post, or remained, on, or at, the frontier (S, Mgh, Sgh, L, K) of the enemy, (S, Msb, K,) or over against the enemy. (Mgh.) And hence, i. e. from this latter application, (AAF, TA,) rAbT AlA^amora , (TK,) inf. n. ribaATN (AAF, K) and muraAbaTapN , (TK,) (assumed tropical:) He kept, or applied himself, constantly, perseveringly, or assiduously, to the thing, or affair. (AAF, K, TK.) It is said in the Kur [ch. iii., last verse], A@SobiruwA waSaAbiruwA waraAbiTuwA Be ye patient in endurance of what your religion requires, and vie ye in patience with your enemy, and persevere ye in fighting against your enemy, (Mgh, TA,) and in tying the horses [ at the
; or, as some say, a simple subst., meaning, in this case, a thing whereby one is tied from acts of disobedience, and restrained from forbidden deeds. (TA.) [See also SaAbara .]

A thing with which one ties, binds, or makes fast, (S, Msb, K,) a skin, (S, Msb,) and a beast, (S,) &c.; (S, Msb;) a rope with which a beast is tied: (Mgh:) pl. rubuTN (S, Msb, K) and ruboTN ; (S, TA;) the latter a contraction of the former: (TA:) and ↓ and ↓ also signify a thing with which a beast is tied. (K.) It is said in a prov., A_ino *ahaba EayorN faEayorN fiY Alr~ibaATi [ If an ass is gone away, an ass is tied to the cord ]: relating to contentment with what is present and relinquishment of what is absent. (Mgh.) [See also

3.] ― -b2- [Hence,] used by the vulgar in the sense of A^uxo*apN , meaning (assumed tropical:) A kind of fascination by which enchantresses withhold their husbands from other women. (TA in art. Ax* .) ― -b3- A snare for catching game. (S, Mgh.) You say, qaTaEa AlZ~aboYu ribaATahu [ The gazelle rent his snare ]. Hence, (TA in art. qrD ,) qaraDa rbaATahu (assumed tropical:) He died: (M and K in that art.:) or he was at the point of death. (K in that art.) (M in that art.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) The spirit: as in the saying of El-'Ajjáj, describing a wild bull, fabaAta wahowa vaAbitu Alr~ibaATi [ And he passed the night firm in spirit ]. (TA.) -A2- See also rabiyTN , (of which it is a pl., or pl. pl.,) in three places. -A3- A single building of those which are called ribaATaAt

Tied, bound, or made fast; as also ↓ ; (K, TA;) applied to a horse, (Mgh,) or similar beast ( daAb~ap ); as also ↓ ; (TA;) applied to the former, i. q. marobuwTN ; (Mgh;) or maAyurotabaTu [which may perhaps signify the same; but more probably, taken to be tied, or for keeping post, on the enemy's frontier ]; (S;) and [in like manner] rabiyTapN , applied to the latter, i. q. maAA@rotubiTa : (K:) and rabiyTN applied to a horse also signifies tied and fed in the court of a house: (TA:) pl. rubuTN (TA) and ↓ , (Mgh,) or the latter is a pl. pl., being pl. of rubuTN . ; or an inf. n. used as a subst., being an inf. n. of rabaTa in the sense of raAbaTa ; (Bd;) or it is an inf. n. of raAbaTa ; and therefore [when used as an epithet, like any inf. n. so used,] is applied to one as well as to a pl. number; (Ham p. 222;) or pl. of rabiyTo : (Bd, Mgh:) or it means of mares: (Fr, TA:) and ribaATN signifies horses; five thereof, and upwards: (S, K:) or horses, themselves, that are taken to be tied, or for keeping post, on the enemy's frontier. [act. part. n. of 1]. ― -b2- xal~afa fulaAnN biAlv~agori jayo$FA raAbiTapF [ Such a one left behind him on the frontier an army having their horses tied in preparation for the enemy

senses.text: 1 signifies The throwing, or casting, of stones: (S, K:) this is its primary meaning: (S, TA:) you say, rajamahu , aor. , inf. n. rajomN , (S, Msb, TA,) He threw, or cast, stones at him

; or pelted him with stones: (S, TA:) or he struck him, or smote him, with rajam , meaning stones: (Msb:) and rujuwmN is syn. with rajomN , as an inf. n.: thus some explain the saying, in the Kur [lxvii. 5], wajoEalonaAhaA rujuwmFA lil$~ayaATiyni [ And we have made them for casting at the devils; meaning shooting stars, which are believed to be hurled at the devils that listen by stealth, beneath the lowest heaven, to the words of the angels therein: but see other explanations below, voce rajomN ]. (TA.) ― -b2-

Hence, (S, TA,) The act of slaying [ in any manner, but generally stoning, i. e. putting to death by stoning ]. (S, K.) So in rajomu Alv~ay~ibayoni A_i*aA zanayaA [ The slaying, or stoning, of the two married persons when they have committed adultery ]. (TA.) ― -b3- [(assumed tropical:) The act of beating, or battering, the ground with the feet.] One says of a camel, yarojumu AlA^aroDa (assumed tropical:) [ He beats, or batters, the ground ], i. e., with his feet; which implies commendation: (TA:) and so one says of a horse; (K;) or yurojumu fiY AlA^aroDi . (S.) And one says also, jaA='a yarojumu , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ He came beating, or battering, the ground
; or] passing along with an ardent and a rapid running. (Lh, K, * TA.) [See also

8.] ― -b4- (tropical:) The act of cursing. (K, TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) The act of reviling. (K, TA.) laA^arojuman~aka , in the Kur xix. 47, means (assumed tropical:) I will assuredly revile thee: (Bd, Jel, TA: see also another explanation below, in this paragraph:) or I will assuredly cast stones at thee, (Bd, Jel,) so that thou shalt die, or shalt remove far from me. (Bd.) And you say, rajamotuhu biAlqawoli , meaning (assumed tropical:) I uttered foul, or evil, speech against him. (Msb.) [See also rajabahu .] ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) The act of driving away; expelling; putting, or placing, at a distance, away, or far away. (K.) ― -b7- (assumed tropical:) The act of cutting off from friendly, or loving communion or intercourse; forsaking

; or abandoning. (K.) ― -b8- Also [as being likened to the throwing of stones, in doing which one is not sure of hitting the mark,] i. q. qa*ofN (K, TA) biAlgayobi (assumed tropical:) [The act of speaking of that which is hidden, or which has not become apparent to the speaker; and conjecturing ]; (TA;) or speaking conjecturally: (S, TA:) and (K, TA) some say (TA) i. q. gayobN [as meaning (assumed tropical:) a doubting ]: (K, TA: [in the CK, AlEayobu is erroneously put for Algayobu :] and Zan~N [which means (assumed tropical:) an opining, or a conjecturing ]. (K, TA.) One says, rajama biAlgayobi (assumed tropical:) He spoke of that which he did not know. (Ham p.
494.) And rajama biAlZ~an~i (Z, TA) (assumed tropical:) He spoke conjecturally: (MA:) or he conjectured, or opined. (Bd in xviii.

Hence, qaAlahu rajomFA (assumed tropical:) He said it conjecturally. (Z, TA.) Hence also, (TA,) rajomFA baAlgayobi , in the Kur [xviii. 21], (S, TA,) (assumed tropical:) [ Speaking conjecturally of that which is hidden, or unknown; as indicated in the S and TA: or] conjecturing in a case hidden from them. ; or] the space which the traveller journeys in about a day: (Msb:) sing. of maraAHilu ; (S, Msb, K;) which is also a pl. of muraH~alN as an epithet applied to a burod . (TA.) senses.text: 1 , [aor. , inf. n. rado'N ,] He supported, propped, or stayed, the wall, (ISh, T, K,) by means of a piece of timber or wood, or a buttress or the like, to prevent its falling; (ISh, T;) as also ↓ : (Yoo, T, K:) or radaA^a AlHaAy^iTa bibinaA='K [ he supported the wall by a structure; ] he attached a structure to the wall. (M.) ― -b2-

Hence, (T,) radaA^ahu bihi He strengthened and supported him, or it, by means of it, (Lth, T, M, * K,) namely, a person by a thing, (Lth, T,) or a thing by a thing, (M,) like as one strengthens and supports a wall by means of a structure which he attaches thereto; (T;) as also ↓ . (T, * K.) And radaA^ahu , (Mgh, TA,) inf. n. rado'N , (Mgh,) He helped, aided, or assisted, him; (Mgh, TA;) as also ↓ : (T, S, M, Msb, K:) and radaA^otuhu and ↓ , (T,) or binafosiY ↓ , (S,) I was, or became, a helper, an aider, or an assistant, to him. (T, S.) ― -b3- Hence also, (i. e., from rdA^ AlHaAy^T ,) radaA^a AlA_ibila (tropical:) He took good care of the camels, (A, K, TA,) in tending and pasturing them. (TA.) -A2- tarosiygN also signifies The making [the means of subsistence] ample, or abundant. (K.) You say, rs~g AlEayo$a He made the means of subsistence ample, or abundant. (TK.) [Or rs~g Ealayohi fiY AlEayo

8.] -A3- rs~gtu kalaAmFA , (JK,) inf. n. as above, (K,) i. q. laf~aqotu bayonahu [meaning I interlarded, or embellished, speech. or discourse, with falsehood: accord. to the TK, connected it, and arranged it, or put it in order: but see the pass. part. n., below]. (JK, K, * TA.)

3 , (Ibn-'Abbád, K,) inf. n. muraAsagapN and risaAgN , (Lth, Ibn-'Abbád, K,) He took hold of his rusog [meaning ankle ] in wrestling with him, the latter doing the like. (Lth, Ibn-'Abbád, K.) One says, raAdagahu vum~a raAsagahu vum~a maAragahu [ He strove with him to throw him down: then he took hold of his ankle &c.: then he rolled with him on the ground, or in the dust ]. (TA.)
8 He expended amply, or abundantly, upon his family, or household. (Ibn-Buzurj, K.) [See also

and ↓ , (S, Msb, K,) of a daAb~ap [or beast of the equine kind], (S, Msb,) [The pastern; i.e.] the slender place [or part ] between the solid hoof and the joint of the waZiyf [or shank ] of the fore leg, and of the hind leg; (S, Msb, K;) or, [in other words,] of solid-hoofed animals, the part that joins the wZyf of each of the fore legs, and of the hind legs, to the hoof; and of camels, the part that joins the A^awoZifap [or shanks ] to the A^axofaAf [or feet ]: (TA:) and (Msb, and so in some copies of the K, but in other copies of the latter “ or, ” [which is more correct, as will be seen from what follows,]) of a human being, [the wrist, and the ankle; i. e.] the joint between the hand and the fore arm, and between the foot and the shank: (Msb, K, TA:) and of any beast ( dAb~h ,) the lik
A laxness in the legs of a camel. (As, S, K.)

A cord, or rope, that is tied (JK, S, K) firmly (S) to the rusog [or pastern ] of the camel, (JK, S, K,) or, accord. to the T, to each rusog , [the dual form being there used, meaning to the pastern of each fore leg, ] of the camel, (TA,) to prevent him from going away; (S, K;) also called ↓ ; of which the pl. is maraAsigu : (JK:) or, as some say, rsaAgN is pl. of ↓ meaning a cord, or rope, with which a camel, and an ass, is [ tethered, or] shackled
; or a string, or cord, with which the rusog [or pastern ] of each of the fore legs of a camel [or an ass ] is tied. (TA.) ― -b2- Also an inf. n. of
Ample, or abundant, means of subsistence: and TaEaAmN rasiygN Much food or wheat. (Aboo-Málik, K.)

sing. of maraAsiygu [probably a mistranscription for maraAsigu ] meaning [ Bracelets of tortoiseshell or horn or ivory, such as are termed ] masak , that are worn by women on their arms; one of which is also called ↓ . (TA.) ― -b2- See also risaAgN .
He is amply, or abundantly, provided for in respect of the means of subsistence. (JK, * TA.) -A2- raA^oYN muras~agN An unsound opinion or counsel or advice. (JK, Ibn- 'Abbád, K.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. and , inf. n. rasofN and rasafaAnN (S, M, O, Msb, K) and rasiyfN , (M, O, Msb, K,) He walked, or went along, in the manner of him who is shackled: (S, M, O, K:) or he walked, or went along, in shackles, gently, softly, or in a leisurely manner: (M:) or you say, rasafa fiY qayodihi he walked, or went along, in his shackles: (MA, Msb:) or he went along [ therein ] by leaps
; or gently. (MA.) rasiyfN also signifies The making short steps. (O.) And rasafa , aor. , He (a camel) went with short steps, raising and putting down his feet quickly. (Aboo-Nasr, O.)

4 , (AZ, S,) inf. n. A_irosaAfN , (K,) I drove along the camels, they being shackled. (AZ, S, K. * [In one of my copies of the S, instead of muqay~adapF , I find muqay~adFA , i.e. I being shackled. ])
8 , inf. n. AirotisaAfN ; (K; so in MS. copies, and so in the CK;) or ↓ , in measure like Aikofahar~a , inf. n., AirotisofaAfN ; (O, and in like manner in the TK;) i. q. AirotafaEa [ It became raised
; or it rose: &c.]. (O, K.)
4 : see what next precedes. [This art. is wanting in the copies of the L and TA to which I have had access.]

senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. rasalN and rasaAla , He (a camel) was, or became, easy in pace. (M, K.) ― -b2-

Also, aor. , inf. n. rasalN (AZ, Az, Msb, K) and rasaAlapN , as above, (AZ, Az, K,) It (hair) became lank, not crisp; (Msb, K;) and so ↓ : (S, K:) or lank and pendent: (Msb:) or long, and lank or pendent. (AZ, Az, Msb.) laA yajibu mina Alb~iHoyapi ↓ means [ The washing ] of what hangs down, and descends, [ of the beard, ] from the chin [ is not requisite, or necessary, or incumbent ]. (Mgh.) -A2- [Golius says, as on the authority of the KL, that rasala signifies Nuncium misit: but what I find in the KL is, that rasuwlN , as an inf. n., signifies the bringing a message ( PygAm brdn ) : whence it seems that rasala means he brought a message. ]

2 , in reading, or reciting, (Msb, K,) i. q. tarotiylN ; (K, TA;) i. e. (TA) Easy [or leisurely ] utterance; without haste: (Yz, Msb, TA:) or, as some say, with consecution of the parts, or portions: (TA:) and ↓ therein signifies the same: (Yz, Msb:) or fiY ↓ qir~A='atihi signifies he proceeded in a leisurely manner in his reading, or reciting, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and was grave, staid, sedate, or calm, (Mgh,) and endeavoured to understand, without raising his voice much. (TA.) It is said in a trad., kaAna fiY kalaAmihi tarosiylN i. e. tarotiylN [ There was in his (Mohammad's) speech an easy, or a leisurely, utterance ]. (TA.) And in another trad. it is said, waA_i*aA A^aqamota faA@Ho*imo ↓ [expl. in art. H*m ]. (Mgh.) -A2- See also 4, last sentence but one. -A3- ras~alotu fuSolaAniY , inf. n

3 (S, MA,) inf. n. muraAsalapN , (S,) He sent a message, and a letter, or an epistle, to him, (MA, PS,) the latter doing the like: (PS:) [ he interchanged messages, and letters, with him. ] You say, rAslhu fiY ka*aA [ He interchanged messages, or letters, with him, in relation to such a thing ]: and bayonahumaA muraAsalaAtN [ Between them two are interchanges of messages, or of letters ]. (TA.) And haYa turaAsilu AlxuT~aAba [ She interchanges messages, or letters, with those who demand women in marriage ]. (M, K.) And turaAsiluhu biAlxuT~aAbi [ She interchanges messages, or letters, with him by means of those who demand women in marriage ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] rAslhu fiY niDaAlK A^awo gayorihi [ He acted interchangeably, or alternated, with him in a competition in shooting, or in some ot

; or he so relieved, or aided, him in singing with a high voice: or rAslhu fiY Eamalihi he aided him, [or relieved him, by alternating with him, ] or he followed him, or imitated him, in his work: (IAar, Msb:) and rAslhu AlginaA='a he emulated him, or imitated him, [ by alternating with him, ] in the singing. (TA.) And rAslhu fiY AlqiraA='ap He aided him, or assisted him, [or relieved him, by alternating with him, ] in the reading, or reciting, of the Kur-án &c. (MA.)

4 signifies The act of sending. (K, KL, &c.) Thus is explained A_irosaAlu A@ll~`hi A^anobiyaA='ahu [i. e. God's sending his prophets. ] (Th, TA.) You say, ↓ (S) I sent such a one with a message. (PS.) And ↓ (MA, Msb *) He sent to him a message, or a letter, (MA,) or a messenger. (Msb.) ― -b2- [The act of sending forth, or starting, a horse for a race: the discharging a thing; as, for instance, an arrow from a bow; and water, or the like, from a vessel &c. in which it was confined: the launching forth a ship or boat; letting it go; letting it take its course: ] the act of setting loose or free; letting loose; loosing, unbinding, or liberating. (K.) You say Arsl Al$~aYo'a He set loose or free, &c., the thing. (M.) And A^arosalotu AlT~aAy^ira mino yadiY I let go, or let loose, the bird from m

; or he abstained from, or neglected, aiding him, or assisting him. (TA.) ― -b5- Also The act of making to have dominion, or authority, and power; making to have, or exercise, absolute dominion or sovereignty or rule, or absolute superiority of power or force
; or giving power, or superior power or force. (M, K.)

Hence, in the Kur [xix. 86], A^arosalonaA Al$~ayaATiyna EalaY AlkaAfiriyna taw^uz~uhumo A^az~FA , i. e. [ We have made the devils to have dominion, &c., over the unbelievers, inciting them strongly to acts of disobedience

; or] we have appointed, or prepared, the devils for the unbelievers, because of their unbelief; like as is said in the same [xliii. 35], nuqay~iDo lahu $ayoTaAnFA [“ We will appoint, or prepare, for him a devil ” as an associate]: this is the preferred explanation: [or it may be well rendered we have sent the devils against the unbelievers: ] some say that the meaning is, we have left the devils to do as they please with the unbelievers, not withholding them, or preserving them, from acceptance from them. (Zj, M.) -A2- ArslwA [from risolN ] They had milk in their cattle: (S:) or their milk became much; as also ↓ , inf. n. tarosiylN : (K:) or the latter signifies their milk and drink became much. (TA.) ― -b2- Also [from rasalN ] They became possessors of herds or flocks. (O, K. *)

5 He acted, or behaved, gently, and deliberately, or leisurely, (M, K, TA,) and with gravity, staidness, sedateness, or calmness. (TA.) Alt~aras~ulu fiY AlA^umuwri is The acting, or behaving, [ gently, and] deliberately, or leisurely, and with gravity, staidness, sedateness, or calmness, in affairs. (TA.) See also 2, in three places. ― -b2- Alt~aras~ulu in riding is The extending one's legs upon the beast so as to let, or make, his clothes hang down loosely upon his legs: and in sitting, the crossing one's legs, and letting, or making, his clothes hang down loosely upon them and around him. (TA.) -A2- trs~lA bayona Alqawomi [ He acted as a rasuwl (or messenger ) between the people ]. (Msb and TA in art. Alk .)
6 They sent, one to another, (MA, Msb, TA,) a message [or messages ], (MA, Msb,) or a messenger [or messengers ]. (Msb.) ― -b2-

Hence, trAslwA fiY AlginaA='i [ They relieved, or aided, one another alternately in singing; ] i. e. they combined in singing, one beginning, and prolonging his voice, but being unable to continue long enough to accomplish the cadence, and therefore pausing, and another then taking up the strain, and then the first returning to the modulation, and so on to the end. (Msb.) laA taraAsula fiY AlA^a*aAni means [in like manner] There shall be no relieving, or aiding, one another [ alternately ], i. e., no combining [ of two or more persons, each performing a part alternately ], in the chanting of the call to prayer. (Msb.) [In other cases likewise] Alt~araAsulu signifies The doing the like of that which one's companion, or fellow, [or another, ] does, in such a manner as that one follows anothe
10 It (a thing) was, or became, loose, or slack; syn. salisa . (M, TA.) ― -b2- Said of hair: see 1, in two places. [In like manner said of a tree, &c., It drooped

; or was pendent. Said of a cheek, (to which its part. n. musotarosilN is applied as an epithet in the K voce A^asiylN ,) It was, or became, lank. ] ― -b3- AlAisotirosaAlu in the pace of a beast is The going gently, deliberately, or leisurely. (TA.) [And you say, Astrslt Ald~aAb~apN The beast went a gentle, deliberate, or leisurely, pace. ] ― -b4-
Also, [in other cases,] The being still, and steady. (TA.) ― -b5-

Hence, (TA,) Astrsl A_ilayohi (tropical:) He acted, or behaved, towards him with freedom, boldness, forwardness, or presumptuousness, and with familiarity; syn. AinobasaTa , and AisotaA^onasa ; (S, K, TA;) and was at ease, and confided in him, with respect to that which he told him: (TA:) or he acted forwardly, or impudently, towards him: he acted forwardly, impudently, freely, or familiarly, towards him, in the way of coquetry, or feigned disdain. (MA.) ― -b6- And Astrsl Ald~ahoru fiyhimo faA^afonaAhumo [(assumed tropical:) Fate made free with them, and destroyed them ]. Easy; applied to a pace. (M, K.) ― -b2- Easy in pace; applied to a he-camel: fem. with p : (S, M, K:) or soft, or gentle, in pace; applied to a he-camel and to a she-camel: (Msb:) and ↓ , also, applied to a she-camel, has the former of these significations; and its pl. is maraAsiylu : (S, K:) or this pl. signifies light, or active, she-camels, that give thee what they have to give spontaneously; and rasolapN is applied to one thereof: a she-camel is termed ↓ as being likened to the arrow thus called. (TA.) ― -b3- Soft, and lax, or flaccid: [app. applied to a he-camel; for it is added,] one says naAqapN rasolapN AlqawaAy^imi , meaning A she-camel loose, or slack, [ in the legs, and] soft in the joints [ thereof ]. (TA. [See also another meaning assigned to this phrase in what follows.]) ― -

Gentleness; and a deliberate, or leisurely, manner of acting or behaving; as also ↓ ; (M, K;) [and perhaps ↓ and ↓ ; for] one says AifoEalo ka*aA waka*aA EalaY risolika (S, Mgh, * Msb, * CK * [but not in my MS. copy of the K nor in the copies used by SM]) and rasolika and rasolatika , (CK, [but likewise wanting in MS. copies of the K,]) i. e. Camels: (M, K:) thus expl. by A'Obeyd, without any epithet: (M:) or a drove, or herd, or a distinct collection or number, of camels, (S, M, * Msb, K,) and of sheep or goats, (S, K,) accord. to ISk from ten to twenty-five, (TA,) or the rasal of the watering-trough is at least ten, and extending to twenty-five; and the word is masc. and fem.; (M;) and also (assumed tropical:) of horses or horsemen; (S;) applied to (tropical:) a company of men (Mgh, Msb) as being likened to a drove, or herd, of camels: (Msb:) and also a distinct collection or number of any things: (M, K:) pl. (M.) ― -b2- And Heaviness, sluggishness, laziness, or indolence: (M, K:) you say rajulN fiyhi rasolapN A man in whom is heaviness, &c. (M.) ― -b3- See also risolN , first sentence.

Hence, as meaning *uw rasuwlK , i. e. *uw risaAlapK [ One who has a message; i. e. a messenger ]; (TA;) i. q. ↓ , (S, M, K,) meaning one sent with a message; (S;) of the measure faEuwlN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN [or rather mufoEalN ]: (Msb:) [and often meaning an apostle of God; and with the article Al especially applied to Mohammad:] accord. to IAmb, its meaning in the proper language of the Arabs is one who carries on by consecutive progressions the relation of the tidings of him who has sent him; taken from the phrase jaA='ati AlA_ibilu rasalFA , meaning “ The camels came following one another: ” and the saying of the Muëdhdhin, A^a$ohadu A^an~a muHam~adFA rasuwlu A@ll~`h means I know [or acknowledge ] and declare that Mohammad is the relater by consecutive progressions of t

4. The saying in the Kur [xxv. 39], waqawoma nuwHK lam~a ka*~abuwA Alr~usula A^agoraqonaAhumo [lit. And the people of Noah, when they charged with lying the apostles, we drowned them ], Zj says, may mean that they charged with lying Noah alone; for he who charges with lying a prophet charges therewith all the prophets, since they believe in God and in all his apostles

; or the general term may be here used as meaning one; like as when you say, A^anota mim~ano yunofiqu Ald~araAhima , meaning “ Thou art of those who expend the kind of things termed drAhm . ” (M.) ― -b3- One says also, Als~ihaAmu rusulu AlmanaAyaA (tropical:) [ Arrows are the messengers of death, or of the decrees of death ]. (TA.) ― -b4- See also the next paragraph.

Easy: occurring in the saying of Jubeyhà El-Asadee, waqumotu rasiylFA biAl~a*iY jaA='a yabotagiY A_ilayohi baliyja Alwajohi lasotu bibaAsiri [ And I undertook, or managed, with ease, that which he came seeking to obtain; bright in countenance to him: I was not frowning ]. (TA.) -A2- Also A stallion-camel (K, * TA) of the Arabian race, that is sent among the $awol [or she-camels that have passed seven or eight months since the period of their bringing forth ] in order that he may leap them: one says, h`*aA rasiylu baniY fulaAnK This is the stallion of the camels of the sons of such a one: and A^arosala banuw fulaAnK rasiylahumo [ The sons of such a one sent the stallion of their camels ]: as though it were of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mufoEalN , from A^arosala . (TA.)

544.) ― -b3- [In the CK and in a MS. copy of the K, voce EamuwdN , it occurs as though meaning The scout, or emissary, or perhaps the advanced guard, of an army: but in other copies of the K, in this instance, accord. to the TA, and in the L, the word is ray^iys .] ― -b4- I. q. ↓ [as meaning one who interchanges messages or letters with another: see 3]. (S, K.) ― -b5- The person who stands with thee ( AlmuwaAqifu laka [in the K (in which this explanation is erroneously assigned to ↓ ) AlmuwaAfiqu laka in a competition in shooting and the like: (M:) [i. e.] rasiylu Alr~ajuli signifies he who stands with the man, ( yaqifu maEahu , Har p. 544,) or he who acts interchangeably, or alternates, with the man, ( yuraAsiluhu , S,) in a competition in shooting, or in some other performance. (S and Ha

; or one who so relieves, or aids, another in singing with a high voice; i. q. mutaAlK : or one who aids another, [or relieves him, by alternating with him, ] or who follows him, or imitates him, in his work. A poet says, (S,) namely El-Ash'ar El-Joafee, (TA,) ↓ biA^an~iY Eano futaAHatikumo ganiY~u [ Now deliver thou to Aboo-' Amr a message, saying that I am in no need of your judging ]: (S:) or baniY EamorKw [ the sons of ' Amr ]: he means, Eano Hukomkumo . (TA.) And hence the saying of Kutheiyir, laqado ka*aba AlwaA$uwna maA buHotu Einodahumo ↓ [ Assuredly the slanderers have lied: I revealed not in their presence a secret, nor did I send them with a message ]: (S, TA:) or, as some relate the second hemistich, (TA,) ↓ [i. e. I revealed not the case of Leyla, nor did I send them with a message ]: thus cited by Th. (M, TA.) ― -b2- risaAlapN also signifies [ A tract, or small treatise or discourse; ] a majal~ap [i. e. book, or writing, relating to science, or on any subject. ] comprising a fe

dim. of rslAt [i. e. risalaAtN ] pl. of risolN [or rather of its syn. risolapN ]: hence the saying, (TA,) A^aloqaY AlkalaAma EalaY rusayolaAtihi , i. e. He held the saying, or speech, in light, or little, or mean, estimation

: see rasuwlN , second sentence. ― -b2- Applied to a tradition ( HadiyvN ), it means (assumed tropical:) Of which the ascription is not traced up so as to reach to its author: (Msb:) [i.e.] AlA^aHaAdiyvu Almurosalapu means the traditions which one relates as on the authority of a taAbiEiY~ , (K TA,) by tracing up the ascription thereof uninterruptedly to him, (TA,) when the tAbEY~ says, “ The Apostle of God ( May God bless and save him ) said, ” without mentioning a SaHaAbiY~ (K, TA) who heard it from the Apostle of God: (TA: [and the like is said in the Mgh:]) maraAsiylu is the [pl. or] quasi-pl. n. of murosalN thus used, [or rather used as a subst., or as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant,] like as manaAkiyru is of munokarN . (Mgh.) And in like manner also, (JK,) raqaA^a AlEiroqu , (Fs, JK, K, TA, [not AlEaraqu , as supposed by Golius and Freytag,]) inf. ns. as above, (K,) The vein stopped or ceased [ bleeding ]; syn. 4 , (S,) or Ald~amoEa , (K,) said of God, (S, K,) He caused his, or the, tears to stop, or cease, flowing; (S, TA;) or caused them to dry up, and to stop, or cease. (K.) The saying laA A^aroqaA^a A@ll~`hu damoEatahu is expl. by El-Mundhiree as meaning May God not remove, or do away with, ( laA rafaEa ,) his tear. (TA.) You say also, A^aroqaA^otu AlEiroqa [meaning I caused the vein to stop or cease bleeding: see 1]. (K, TA.)

; or a thing that is put upon blood for the purpose of stanching it, or stopping its flowing: (S, K:) a subst. from raqaA^a . (Msb.) (S, Msb, K, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] rajulN raquwo'N bayona Alqawomi (assumed tropical:) A man who is a reconciler of the people
; or a peacemaker between them: and [so] raquwo'N limaA bayonahumo , a phrase used by a poet. (TA.)

Hence, said of a captive, He stretched out his neck on the occasion of slaughter, like the bird expanding his wings. (TA.) ; or animal spirit; ] a subtile vaporous substance, which is the principle of vitality and of sensation and of voluntary motion; also called the ruwH HayawaAniY~ ; (KT in explanation of the term nafosN ;) or a subtile body, the source of which is the hollow of the corporeal heart, and which diffuses itself into all the other parts of the body by means of the pulsing veins, or arteries: (KT in explanation of the term Alr~uwHu AlHayawaAniY~u : [so too nafosN ; q. v.: see also Gen. ix. 4: many of the ancients believed the soul to reside in the blood: see Aristotle, De Anim. i. 2, and Virgil's Æn. ix. 349:]) or the vital principle in man: (Fr, TA:) or the breath which a man breathes, and which pervades the whole body: [and this seems to be the original idea expressed by the word:] after its ex

2 and xl. 15: so called because it quickens from the death of infidelity, and thus is, to a man, like the ruwH which is the vital principle of his body: (T:) or (so says Zj accord. to the L, but in the K “ and ” ) the prophetic commission. senses.text: 1 , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. yariybu , (M, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. rayobN (T, M, Mgh, Msb, &c.) and riybapN , (M, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (S, Msb,) It (a thing) occasioned in me disquiet, disturbance, or agitation, of mind: (Ksh and Bd in ii. 1:) [this is the primary signification; (see riybapN ;) a signification also borne by ↓ ; (see the verses of Khálid cited in this paragraph;) whence the other significations here expl. in what follows:] it (a thing) made me to doubt: (Msb: and in like manner raAbahu is expl. in the Mgh:) or it (a thing, M) caused me to have what is termed riybap [i. e. doubt, or suspicion or evil opinion, or doubt combined with suspicion or evil opinion ]; as also ↓ : (M, K: in both of which this meaning is indicated, but not expressed:) but the latter is said

4 , as a trans. verb: see 1, in eight places. -A2- As intrans., it signifies He (a man) was, or became, one in whom was something occasioning doubt, or suspicion or evil opinion, or doubt combined with suspicion or evil opinion; i. e. SaAra *aA riybapi : (Sb, T, S, M:) and he did a thing that occasioned doubt, or suspicion &c.: (As, T:) it is said when one is told something of a person, or thinks it, or imagines it: (Msb:) see 1, in the former half of the paragraph; and also, in three places, in the latter part of the same paragraph. Also It (a thing, or an affair, or a case,) was, or became, one in which was something occasioning doubt, or suspicion &c.; i. e. SaAra *aA rayobK (T, K) or *A riybapK . (M.)

(TA.) ― -b2- [It often means particularly He was sceptical in matters of religion. ]

Want, or need. (TA.)

Hence, in a trad., maA rabukumo A_ilayohi What is [the reason of] your want of him? or your wanting to ask him? (TA.) And, in another trad., maA raAbuka A_ilaY qaToEihaA What is [the reason of] thy wanting to cut it off? thus, says El-Khattábee, they relate it, with damm to the b : but IAth says that it is properly maA A^arabuka , meaning the same: or, accord. to Aboo-Moosà, the right reading may be mA raAbaka , expl. in the preceding paragraph. (TA.)

is an inf. n. of 1, (T, M, Mgh, Msb, &c.,) as also ↓ , (M, K,) or the latter is a simple subst.: (S, Msb:) the primary signification of the latter [and of the former also when it is used as a simple subst.] is Disquiet, disturbance, or agitation, of mind: (Ksh and Bd in ii. 1:) [and hence] the former signifies doubt; (T, S, Msb;) as also ↓ the latter; (S, Mgh;) because doubt disquiets, or disturbs, the mind: (Ksh and Bd ubi suprà, and Mgh:) and opinion; syn. Zan~N : (Msb:) and ↓ the latter, (S, M, A, Mgh, K,) and the former also, (M, A, K,) doubt, or suspicion or evil opinion; syn. tuhamapN (S, M, A, Mgh, K) and Zin~apN : (M, A, K:) or the former, [and ↓ the latter also,] doubt combined with suspicion or evil opinion: (IAth, TA:) and a thing, or an event, or a case, that occasions one doub

Hence, rayobu Alz~amaAni The accidents, or evil accidents, of time, (Ksh and Bd ubi suprà, [in Fleischer's ed. of the latter riyab AlzmAn , which is more agreeable with the explanation, but rayob AlzmAn is more usual,]) that disquiet, or disturb, the minds and hearts: (Ksh:) and rayobu Almanuwni (S, A) [which likewise signifies] the accidents, or evil accidents, of time: (S:) and rayobu Ald~ahori signifies the same; i. e. Sarofuhu , (M, K,) or Suruwfuhu , (T, Msb,) and HawaAdivuhu . (T. [This is said in the TA to be tropical; but I do not find it so characterized in the A.]) ― -b3- [

Hence, likewise,] rayobN also signifies A want; a needful, or requisite, thing, affair, or business; syn. HaAjapN . (S, A, Msb, K.) A poet says, (S,) namely, Kaab Ibn-Málik El-Ansáree, (TA,) qaDayonaA mino tihaAmapa kul~a rayobK wa xayobara vum~a A^ajoyayonaA Als~uyuwfaA [ We accomplished, from Tihámeh, every want, and from Kheyber: then we gave rest to our swords ]. (S.) -A2- [ ryb mentioned by Freytag as applied in art. dls of the S to a certain plant, and written rayob in both of my copies of the S in that art., is a mistake for rabab , which is the reading in the TA, pl. of rib~apN .]

[act. part. n. of 1; Causing, or occasioning, doubt, or suspicion or evil opinion, &c.] IAar says that Aboo-Bekr is related to have said, in his charge to 'Omar, Ealayoka biAlr~aAy^ibi mina AlA^umuwri wa A_iy~aAk wa Alr~aAy^iba minohaA , which Th explains as meaning Keep thou to what is clear, free from dubiousness or confusedness, of affairs, and beware thou of, or avoid thou, what has in it dubiousness, or confusedness, thereof: (T, TA:) the first is from raAba of which the aor. is yaruwbu , said of milk; and the second is from raAba of which the aor. is yariybu . (TA.) [See also a verse cited voce raAy^ibN in art. rwb , and my remark thereon.]

, applied to a man, (T, S, A,) and to a thing or an event, (M, A,) i. q. *uw riybapK [expl. above, voce rayobN ]. (T, S, M, A.) Doubting [or suspecting ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- [It often means particularly Sceptical, or a sceptic, in matters of religion. -A2- And murotaAbN fiyhi , or bihi , Doubted of, or suspected. ]

A space, or measure, [ of time, ] syn. qadorN , (T, Msb,) or miqodaArN ; (A, K;) or a time, a while, syn. saAEapN . (Mgh.) senses.text: 1 , (S, A, Msb,) aor. , (S,) inf. n. zaj~N , (S, A, Msb, K,) He pierced him, or thrust him, (i. e. a man, S, Msb,) with the zuj~ [or pointed iron foot of the spear ]; (S, A, Msb, K; *) and cast at him with it: and zaj~a also signifies he pierced, or thrust, with haste. (TA.) And zajajotuhu biAlr~umoHi I cast at him with the spear. (A, and Ham p.

147.) ― -b2- [Hence,] zaj~a biAl$~aYo'i (tropical:) He cast, or threw, the thing from himself: (A:) or zaj~a biAl$~aYo'i mino yadihi , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. as above, (K, TA,) (tropical:) he cast, or threw, the thing from his hand. (K, * TA.) ― -b3- [And hence,] zaj~N signifies also (tropical:) The running or the ostrich. (K, TA.) You say of the ostrich, zaj~a birijolayohi , (A, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) He ran, (A, TA,) throwing out his legs. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence also,] nazalonaA biwaAdK yazuj~u Aln~abaAta (tropical:) We alighted in a valley putting forth herbage; as though casting it from itself. (A, TA.) ― -b5- See also
4. -A2- zaj~a , sec. pers. zajijota , aor. , inf. n. zajajN , It (an eyebrow) was, or became, narrow and long: (TK:) or arched: (MA:) [or narrow and long and full and arched: see zajajN below.]

4. -A2- zaj~ajato HaAjibahaA , (S, A,) or zj~j HaAjibahu , (K, TA,) inf. n. tazojiyjN , (TA,) She, or he, made her, or his, eyebrow narrow and long: (S, K:) [or made it arched: (see 1, last sentence:) or made it narrow and long and arched: (see zajajN below:)] or clipped the redundant portions of the hair thereof: or lengthened it [ in appearance ] with A_ivomid [i. e. antimony, or ore of antimony, or a black collyrium; like as the ancient Egyptians were accustomed to do, as appears from their paintings and sculptures; and like as some of the Arab women still do; extending a black line towards the ear, and also a similar line from the outer angle of the eye]. (TA.) In the following verse of the poet Er-Rá'ee, A_i*aA maA AlgaAniyaAtu xarajona yawomFA wazaj~ajona AlHawaAjiba waAlEuyuwnaA [th

Hence, from tazojiyHu AlHawaAjibi as signifying “ the clipping of the redundant portions of the hair of the eyebrows, ” zj~j mawoDiEahaA , occurring in a trad., referring to a hole made in a piece of wood in which a thousand deenars and a writing had been inserted, is expl. as meaning He made even, and adjusted, the place thereof: or, accord. to IAth, it may be that the hole was in the end of the piece of wood, and so it may mean he made a zuj~ [q. v.] upon the place thereof, to hold it fast, and to preserve what was in it. (TA.)

4 ; (IAar, ISk, S, A, K;) and ↓ ; (A, TA;) and ↓ , aor. , inf. n. zaj~N ; (Msb;) and zaj~aAhu ; (TA;) He put, or made, a zuj~ [q. v.] to the spear. (IAar, ISk, S, A, Msb, K.) ― -b2- The first of these phrases is said also to signify He removed, or took off, its zuj~ from the spear: (A:) IAar is related to have said thus; but he is also related to have said that this signification is not allowable. (TA.)
8 , said of the eyebrow, It reached to the outer extremity ( *unaAbaY ) of the eye. (K.) ― -b2- And, said of herbage, Its intervening spaces became closed up. (TA.)

[The pointed iron foot, or heel, or shoe, of a spear; ] the iron at the lower extremity of a spear; (S, A, Msb, K;) i. e. the iron which is fixed upon the lower extremity of a spear, and with which the spear is stuck into the ground: the iron which is fixed upon its upper extremity, and with which one pierces, being called sinaAnN : (ISd, TA:) pl. [of mult.] zijaAjN and zijajapN (S, Msb, K) and [of pauc.] A^azojaAjN and A^azij~apN , (TA,) or this last is not allowable, (S, Msb, TA,) accord. to ISk. (Msb.) Zuheyr says, wamano yaEoSi A^aToraAfa Alz~ijaAji faA_in~ahu yuTiyEu AlEawaAliY ruk~ibato kul~a laho*ami [ And he who refuses to yield to the points of the iron feet of the spears shall yield to the upper extremities thereof mounted with every sharp spear-head ]: ISk says, he means that he

Hence, as being likened to the zuj~ of the spear, (L,) (tropical:) The extremity of the elbow, (S, L, K,) which is pointed: (L:) or the part [or joint ] between the lower extremity of the os humeri and the extremity of the ulna at the elbow: (T in art. Abr :) or [simply] the elbow. (A.) You say, Ait~akaA^a EalaY zuj~ayohi (tropical:) He leaned upon his elbows: and Ait~akaw^uwA EalaY zijaAji maraAfiqihimo (tropical:) [ They leaned upon the extremities of their elbows ]. (A.) ― -b3- [Hence also, (tropical:) A tush, or canine tooth: ] zijaAju AlfaHoli signifies (tropical:) the tushes of the stallion-camel. (A, K.) ― -b4- [Hence also a signification mentioned by Golius on the authority of Meyd, (assumed tropical:) An iron pivot (“ subscus ferrea ”) round which a mill-stone turns. ] ― -b5- Also

Narrowness and length in the eyebrows: (S, K:) or narrowness and archedness of the eyebrows: (A:) or archedness thereof: (MA:) or narrowness and length and fulness and arched- ness thereof. (TA.) [See 1, last sentence.] ― -b2-

Also, in an ostrich, (assumed tropical:) Length of the shanks, and width of step. (L.) ― -b3- And in camels, (assumed tropical:) Width, or wideness, ( rawaHN ) in [ the space between ] the hind legs. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) Wideness of a solid hoof: which is a fault. (TA in art. Sr .)

Darts, or javelins, ( HiraAbN ,) furnished with iron heads: (K:) its sing. is not mentioned. (TA.) ― -b2- [It is also expl. in different copies of the K as meaning HamiyrN muqotatilapN or muqat~alapN or muqotal~apN : the first I regard as the right reading; i. e. Asses ( wild asses ) fighting one another. ]

and zajaAjN and zijaAjN , (AO, S, Msb, K,) the first of which is that used by the seven readers [of the Kur-án], (Msb,) and the last is the least common, (TA,) words of well-known meaning; (S, Msb, K;) [ Glass: pieces of glass: glassvessels: ] glass flasks or bottles; syn. qawaAriyru : (TA:) and [ glass ] drinking-cups or bowls: (AO, TA:) pls. of ↓ (AO, S) and ↓ and ↓ : (AO:) or [rather] these are the ns. un. (Msb.) In the Kur [xxiv. 35], ↓ means A lamp, syn. qinodiyl ,(Lth, Bd, Jel,) of zujaAj [i. e. glass ]. (Bd.) -A2- zajaAjN , with fet-h, also signifies The berries of the clove-tree; syn. Hab~u Alqaranofuli . (Ktr, TA.)

and zajaAjapN and zijaAjapN : see the next preceding paragraph; the first, in two places. -A2- The last also signifies The art, or occupation, of making zujaAj [i. e. glass, glass vessels, &c.]. (TA.)
(Msb, K, TA) [and zajaAjiY~N and zijaAjiY~N , the former in the CK, and both implied in the K and in the Msb,] A seller of zajaAj [i. e. glass, glass vessels, &c.]. (Msb, K.)
A maker, or manufacturer, of zujaAj [i. e. glass, glass, vessels, &c.] (Msb, K.)
(assumed tropical:) The anus; because it emits ( tazuj~u ) wind and excrement. (TA.)

, applied to a man, (S, A,) Having narrow and long eyebrows: (S, K:) or having narrow and arched eyebrows: (A:) [or having arched eyebrows : see zajajN :] or having narrow and long and full and arched eyebrows: (TA:) fem. zaj~aA='u , (A, K,) applied to a woman: (A:) [pl. zuj~N :] and one says also A^azaj~u AlHawaAjibi [meaning the same]. (L.) It is likewise applied to the eyebrow [as meaning Narrow and long: or narrow and arched: &c.]: (A, TA:) and so ↓ : (TA:) or the former signifies an eyebrow narrow and long [&c.] naturally: and ↓ the latter, rendered so artificially. (MF.) And AlA^azaj~u is a name for The eyebrow [itself] in the dial. of El-Yemen. (TA.) ― -b2-

Also, applied to a male ostrich, (assumed tropical:) Long in step: (S, K:) or longlegged and long in step: (L:) or that runs throwing out his legs: (TA:) or having white feathers above his eyes: (K:) fem. zaj~aA='u : (S:) and pl. zuj~N (K.) And, applied to a man, (assumed tropical:) Long-legged. (L.) ― -b3-
Also, applied to a solid hoof, (assumed tropical:) Wide. (TA in art. Sr . [See zajajN , last sentence.])
A spear having a zuj~ [q. v.] affixed to it. (ISk, S.)
A short spear, like the mizoraAq , (S, K, TA,) having at its lower extremity a zuj~ [q. v.]: and sometimes used as meaning one that transpierces, or passes through, quickly. (TA.)
An instrument with which the eyebrow is made such as is termed A^azaj~u [or narrow and long, or narrow and arched, &c.]. (TA.)
: see A^azaj~u in two places.

Pierced, or thrust, with the zuj~ [q. v.] of a spear. (S, TA.) And Cast at therewith. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A large bucket ( garobN ) not made round, but having its two lips [or opposite edges ] put together, and then sewed. (K.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. zajorN , (S, A, Msb,) He chid him, by a cry, by his voice, or by reproof: (S, * K, * TA:) he checked him, restrained him, or forbade him, with rough speech: (TA:) or prevented, hindered, restrained, or withheld, him: or forbade, or prohibited, him: [ by any kind of cry or speech: ] as also ↓ ; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) the latter originally Aztjrhu : (Msb, TA:) Eano ka*aA from [ doing ] such a thing: (A, * Mgh, TA:) and Eani Als~uwo'i from evil. (TA.) ― -b2- zajara Alkaloba , (K,) and Als~abuEa , (TA,) and zajara bihi (K,) (assumed tropical:) He cried out to, or at, the dog, (K,) and the beast of prey, (TA,) in order that he might forbear, refrain, or abstain. (K, TA.) [See a tropical ex. voce HinowN .] ― -b3- zajara AlbaEiyra (tropical:) He in

Hence, (A,) zajorN also signifies (tropical:) The auguring from the flight, alightingplaces, cries, kinds, or names, of birds: (S, A, K:) you say, huwa yazojuru AlT~ayora He augurs from the flight, &c., of birds: (A:) or zajorN signifies the auguring well from a bird's or some other thing's sunuwH [or turning the right side towards one, or the contrary ], and evil from its buruwH [or turning the left side towards one, or the contrary ]. (Zj.) And zajara guraAba Albayoni means (assumed tropical:) He went away, departed, or journeyed. (Har p.

308.) ― -b8- [Hence,] it also signifies (tropical:) The practising of divination: (K:) or a species thereof: you say, zajarotu A^an~ahu yakuwnu ka*aA waka*aA I have divined that it is so and so. (S, L.) [See also zaAjirN ] ― -b9- zajarato bimaA fiY baTonihaA (assumed tropical:) She (a camel) cast forth what was in her belly. (K, TA.)
6 [ They checked, restrained, or forbade, one another, with rough speech
; or] they prevented, hindered, or withheld one another
; or they forbade, or prohibited, one another; from abominable, foul, or evil, conduct. (A, Msb.)
7 and ↓ He, being chidden, by a cry, by the voice, or by reproof
; or being checked, restrained, or forbidden, with rough speech; (TA;) or being prevented, hindered, restrained, or withheld

; or being forbidden or prohibited; refrained, forbore, or abstained; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) Eano ka*aA from [ doing ] such a thing. (Mgh, TA.) ― -b2- ↓ , in the Kur liv. 9, means He was driven away. (TA.) ― -b3- Anzjr He (a dog) became urged, or incited, by a cry, to pursue the game. (Mgh.)
8 , for Aizotajara , trans. and intrans.: see
1 and 7; each in two places.

1. (S, A, Msb.) ― -b2- A crying at camels [ &c. ], and an urging or inciting of them. (TA.) ― -b3- A cry by which one chides, i. e., either checks or urges, a beast &c.; like Saho to a man, and Eadaso to a mule, &c. (The lexicons, passim.) -A2- See also what next follows.

(Az, O, K) and ↓ (IDrd, O, K) Large fish, (K,) [i. e.] a species of large fish, (IDrd, O,) with small scales: (TA:) IDrd says, thus called by the people of El-'Irák, but I do not think the appellation to be genuine Arabic: (O:) pl. zujuwrN . (O, K.)

(tropical:) A she-camel that will not yield her milk abundantly until chidden: (A, K, TA:) or that yields her milk abundantly to her young one if beaten, but does not if let alone: (TA:) or (K, TA, but accord. to the CK “ and ”) a she-camel that knows [ her young one ] with her eye, but repudiates it with her nose [ when she smells it ]: (S, K:) and a she-camel that inclines to the young one of another, and not to her own, but only smells it, and refuses to yield her milk to it; syn. EaluwqN . (K.) ― -b2- It is also applied, metaphorically, as an epithet to war. (A, TA.)
[ One who chides, &c., much, or often. ]

[act. part. n. of 1]. ― -b2- [Hence,] kafaY biAlquroA=ni zaAjirFA (tropical:) [ The Kur-án suffices as a chider, checker, restrainer, or forbidder ]. (A, TA.) And Alz~aAjiru (assumed tropical:) The exhorter, on the part of God, in the heart of the believer; i. e. the light shed into it, [or what we term the light of nature, ] that invites him to the truth. (KT.) ― -b3- Alz~aAjiraAtu , in the Kur xxxvii. 2, means (tropical:) The angels who are the drivers of the clouds. (K, * TA.) ― -b4- zaAjirN also signifies (tropical:) A diviner; because, when he sees that which he thinks to be of evil omen, he cries out with a high, or loud, and vehement, voice, forbidding to undertake the thing in question. (Zj, TA.) ― -b5- A^abuw zaAjirK (assumed tropical:) The crow; because one augurs by means of it.

[ a subst. formed from the epithet zaAjirN by the addition of p . Its pl. occurs in the saying,] kar~irato EalaY samoEihi AlmawaAEiZu waAlz~awaAjiru (tropical:) [ Exhortations, and chiding or restraining speeches, were repeated in his ears ]. (A, TA.)
and zinojiyrapN : see art. znjr .
A camel having a looseness in the vertebræ of his back, arising from disease, or from galls, or sores, produced by the saddle: (O, K: *) [or having a fracture in his back; ] like A^axozalu . (O.)

[ A place of zajor , i. e. chiding, &c.]. ― -b2- [Hence,] huwa min~iY mazojara Alkalobi , an elliptical phrase, meaning (tropical:) [ He is, in relation to me, or min~iY is here used in the sense of EinodiY , i. e., in my estimation, ] as though he were in the mzjr of the dog; (Sb, TA;) [i. e., as though he were to be chidden like the dog, and driven away; ] said by Z to be tropical. (TA.)

[ A cause of zajor , i. e. chiding, &c.: a noun of the same class as maboxalapN &c.; pl. mazaAjiru ]. A poet says, mano kaAna laA yazoEumu A^an~iY $aAEiru faloyadonu min~iY tanohahu AlmazaAjiru i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He who will not assert that I am a poet, let him approach me: ] preventing causes forbid him. (TA.) And one says, *ikoru A@ll~`hi mazojarapN lil$~ayoTaAni (tropical:) [ The remembrance, or the mention, of God is a cause of driving away the devil ]. (A, TA.)

, in the Kur liv. 4, (Bd, TA,) is [an inf. n.,] syn. with AizodijaArN , (Bd,) meaning (assumed tropical:) Depulsion, and prevention, or prohibition, from the commission of sinful actions; (TA;) or from punishment: or it there means a threatening: and some read maz~ajarN , changing the d into z , and incorporating it [into the preceding letter]. (Bd.)

senses.text: 1 , (MA, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. zajalN , (MA, K, KL, and Har p. 240,) He uttered his voice, or a cry

; or made a sound, or cry: (MA, KL:) or he raised his voice, (K, Har,) to evince emotion. (Har.) ― -b2- [It seems to be indicated in the K that it signifies also He played, or sported: and He, or it (i. e. a company of men), raised cries, shouts, noises, a clamour, or confused cries or shouts or noises: and He trilled, or quavered, and prolonged his voice
; or prolonged it, and modulated it sweetly. See the next paragraph.]

inf. n. of zajila : (MA, K:) [and used as a simple subst:] i. q. SawotN [as an inf. n., meaning The uttering of the voice, or of a sound, or cry: or, as a simple subst., a voice, sound, or cry ]: (S:) or a high, or loud, voice: such have the angels when celebrating the praises of God: (TA:) [and] a vehement sound. (Ham p.
627.) [Hence,] saHaAbN *uw zajalK Clouds having a thundering: (TA:) [and] so ↓ . (S.) ― -b2- A clamour

; or a confusion, or mixture, of cries or shouts or noises, or of crying or shouting or noise. (K.) ― -b3- [ A low, or faint, sound: hence,] zajalu Aljin~i means EaziyfuhaA [i. e. The low, or faint, sound of the jinn, or genii, that is heard by night in the deserts; and said to be a sound like drumming: or the sound of the winds in the atmosphere, imagined by the people of the desert to be the sound of the jinn ]. (TA.) ― -b4- A trilling, or quavering, and prolonging of the voice

; or a prolonging of the voice, and modulating it sweetly. (K.) A poet likens it to the voice of one urging on camels by singing to them, and to the playing on a reedpipe. (Sb, TA.) ― -b5- Also Play, or sport. (K.) ― -b6- And A species of verse, well known; [ a vulgar sort of unmeasured song or balled; ] in this sense post-classical. (TA.)

Raising his voice; as also ↓ . (K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] saHaAbN zajilN : see zajalN And gayovN zajilN Rain accompanied by the sound of thunder. (TA.) And nabotN zajilN A plant, or herbage, in which, or among which, the wind makes a sound. (K.)
: see the next paragraph, in two places.

The sound, or voice, or noise, of men; as also ↓ . (K.) ― -b2- And A company, a collection, or an assemblage: (K:) or a party, or company, of men, (S, K,) peculiarly: (TA:) as also ↓ : (K:) pl. of the former zujalN . (S.)

: see zajilN . ― -b2- It is also applied to a song, or singing, [meaning Loud, ] in the saying, wahuwa yugan~iyhaA ginaA='F zaAjilaA [ And he sings to her, or to them (probably referring to camels), with a loud song or singing ]. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, K,) aor. yazojuw , (S,) inf. n. zajaA='N (S, K, and Ham p. 78) and zajowN (K and Ham) and zujuw~N , (K,) It (a thing) went, or became urged on or along, quickly. (Ham ubi suprà: there indicated by the context, but not expressed.) ― -b2- It (a bad piece of money) passed, or had currency. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b3- It (an affair) was, or became, easy; and right, in a right state, or right in its direction or tendency. (K, TA.) Hence the trad., laA tazojuw SalaApN laA yuqoraA^u fiyhaA bifaAtiHapi AlkitaAbi i. e. [ A prayer in which the opening chapter of the Book (meaning the Kur-án) is not recited ] will not be right. (TA.) ― -b4-

Also, inf. n. zajaA='N , said of the [tax called] xaraAj , It was, or became, easy of collection. (S.) ― -b5- zajaA='N also signifies The acting with penetrative energy, and effectiveness, in an affair. (S, K.) One says, h`*aA AlA^amoru qado zajawonaA Ealayohi [app. meaning This affair, we have effected it, or accomplished it; like as one says, maDayonaA EalaY AlA^amori ]. (T, TA.) And EaTaA='N qaliylN yazojuw xayorN mino kaviyrK laA yazojuw [ A small gift that is effective is better than much that will not be effective ]. (S.) -A2- One says also, DaHika Hat~aY zajaA i. e. [ He laughed until ] his laughing became stopped, or cut short. (S, K. *) -A3- See also what next follows, in two places.

2 , (S, Msb, TA,) inf. n. tazojiyapN , (S, TA,) He pushed it gently, (S, Msb, TA,) in order that it might go on; as also ↓ ; and ↓ , aor. yazojuwhu , inf. n. zajowN : and this last, he drove it, or urged it on, gently; (TA;) [and so zj~Ahu and ↓ , as will be shown by what follows:] or ↓ signifies [simply] he drove it, or urged it on: and he pushed it: and so [app. in both of these senses] zj~Ahu and ↓ . (K.)

Hence, i. e. from zaj~ayotuhu meaning “ I pushed it gently, ” (Har p. 304,) one says, kayofa tuzaj~iY AlA^ay~aAma (S, Har) i. e. kayofa tudaAfiEuhaA [ How dost thou strive with the days in pushing them on, or making them to pass away? ]: (S:) or kyf tadofaEuhaA [ how dost thou push on the days? and thus may mean also kyf tdAfEhA ]: (Har:) [or how dost thou make the days to pass away? for] zj~Y AlA^ay~aAma means he made the days to pass away: (MA:) [or how dost thou pass the days? for it is also said that] tazojiyapN signifies the passing [one's] days. (KL.) [ zj~Y AlA^ay~aAma may be well rendered He made the days to pass away by means of exertion; and so dafaEahaA and daAfaEahaA . Har (ubi suprà) uses the phrase A^uzaj~iY A^ay~aAmFA musowad~apF as meaning I push on evil and hard days. ] ↓

5.]) One says also AlA_ibila ↓ I drove the camels. (S.) And waladahaA ↓ The [ wild ] cow drives her young one. (S.) Alr~iyHu Als~aHaAba ↓ The wind drives along the clouds: (S:) or drives along gently the clouds; as also tuzaj~iyhi , but in an intensive sense. (Msb.) In like manner, saHaAbFA ↓ is said of God, in the Kur [xxiv. 43]: and in the same [xvii. 68], rab~ukumu A@l~a*iY lakumu A@lofuloka fiY AlbaHori ↓ [ Your Lord is He who driveth along for you the ship in the sea ]. (TA.) And a poet says, ↓ i. e. [ I drove him with speech, and ] urged him on: for AizodajaAhu signifies saAqahu [like zaj~aAhu &c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- And zj~Y HaAjatiY He made easy the attainment of my want. (TA.) -A2- zj~Y Alr~umoHa i. q. A^azaj~ahu q. v. in art. zj . (TA in that art.)
4 see 2, in ten places. AzjY also signifies He made money, or bad money, to pass, or be current. (Er-Rághib, TA.)
5 I contented myself with such a thing: a rájiz says, tazaj~a mino dunoyaAka biAlbalaAgi [ Content thyself with what is sufficient of thy worldly possessions ]. (S. [See also
8 see 2, near the end of the paragraph.

More penetrating and effective in an affair than another: (S, K:) so in the saying, fulaAnN A^azojaY bih`*aA AlA^amori mino fulaAnK [ Such a one is more penetrating and effective in this affair than such a one ]. (S, K. *)
, applied to a horse [or other beast], That is driven, or urged on, ( yzjY , [i. e. yuzojaY ,]) in his pace, by little and little. (Ham p.

158.) ― -b2- A small, or scanty, thing; (S, Er-Rághib, TA;) or such as is mean, or paltry; that may be pushed and driven away because of the little account that is made of it. (Er-Rághib, TA.) biDaAEapN muzojaApN means Small, or scanty, merchandise; little in quantity: (S, K:) and so it is said to mean in the Kur [xii. 88]: or, as in some copies of the S, little, or mean, or paltry, merchandise: (TA:) or mean, or paltry, merchandise, rejected by every one to whom it is offered: (A, TA:) or merchandise wherewith the days are pushed on ( tudofaEu [i. e. made to pass away by means of exertion ]) because of its scantiness: (Msb, TA: [for muzojaApN bihaA :]) or, accord. to the shereef El-Murtadà, merchandise driven along portion after portion, scantily and feebly: (TA:) or merchandise in respec

Weak: so termed because of his lagging behind, and requiring to be urged on: (Ham p. 441:) or anything not perfect in nobility, nor in any other praiseworthy quality: or, as some say, one driven to generosity against his will: (TA:) and also, (TA,) applied to a man, i. q. muzal~ajN [q. v., app. here meaning deficient in manliness, or manly virtue, or the like ]. (S, TA.) [ Alz~amaAnu Almuzaj~aY , a phrase used by Har, is expl. (p. 429) as meaning Haq~uhu A^ano yuzaj~iyhi Aln~aAsu , i. e. Time that requires men to push it on, or to make it to pass away by means-of exertion. ]

[The verb is doubly trans.: when the second objective complement is implied, the phrase generally means God caused the means of subsistence to come to him; i. e., gave him, granted him, or bestowed upon him, the means of subsistence

; or supplied, provided, or blessed, him therewith: when the second objective complement is expressed, this word is generally one signifying the means of subsistence or the like, property, or offspring.] One says also, razaqa AlT~aAy^iru faroxahu , aor. , inf. n. razoqN , [ The bird fed its young one. ] (TA.) And razaqa AlA^amiyru Aljunoda The commander gave their subsistence-money, pay, or allowances, to the army: and razaqa Aljunoda razoqapF He gave the army their subsistence-money, &c., once: and ruziquwA razoqatayoni They were given their subsistence-money, &c., twice. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence ruziqa also signifies It (a place) was rained upon. ] Lebeed says, ruziqato maraAbiyEa Aln~ujuwmi waSaAbahaA wadoqu Alr~awaAEidi jawoduhaA warihaAmuhaA meaning muTirato ; (TA;) i. e. 141.) ― -b3- And razaqa fulaAnFA He thanked such a one; was thankful, or grateful, to him

One says, faEalotu *`lika lam~aA razaqotaniY i. e. lam~aA $akarotaniY [ I did that since, or because, thou thankedst me ]. (TA.) And hence, in the Kur [lvi. 81], watajoEaluwna rizoqakumo A^an~akumo taka*~ibuwna [ And do ye make your thanking to be that ye disacknowledge the benefit received, as being from God?]; (K;) i. e., accord. to Ibn-'Arafeh, do ye, instead of acknowledging what God has bestowed upon you, and being thankful for it, attribute it to another than Him? or, accord. to Az and others, [as J also says in the S,] the meaning is, tajoEaluwna $akora riziqokumu Alt~ako*iyba [ do ye make the thanking for your sustenance to be disacknowledgment? ]: (TA:) and some read $akorakumo [for rizoqakumo ]

alphabetical letter The eleventh letter of the alphabet; commonly called zaAYN , and sometimes zaA='N , [and zFA , and zaA , (see zaAYN in art. zwY ,)] and zaY~N , and zaYo . (MF.) It is one of the letters termed majohuwrap [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, and not with the breath only]; and of the letters termed A^asilay~ap , because proceeding from the tip of the tongue. (TA.) Az says that it is not conjoined with S in any Arabic word. (TA.) It is substituted for s and for S ; as in yazodilu for yasodilu , and yazoduqu for yaSoduqu : and in the Tes-heel it is said that it is sometimes interchanged [with s ] after j , as in jusotu xilaAla Ald~iyaAri for juzotu ; and after r , as in rasaba and razaba : which interchange, accord. to MF, is said to be of the dial. of Kelb
; or, as Et-Toosee says, of the dial. of 'Odhrah and Kaab and Benul-' Ambar. (TA.) -A2- [As a numeral, z denotes Seven. ]
